name: MUSES8920 / MUSES8920A
tagline: New JRC's affordable JFET MUSES, the 'budget MUSES01': a clean, grain-free upgrade over NE5532/NJM4580.

lineage.note: Launched 2011, J-FET sibling of MUSES8820 (2010). A 'mass-production' MUSES; layout and lead-frame reportedly simplified for cost.
Took over after the 2022 merger. Replaced MUSES8920 with MUSES8920A (reportedly March 2024); MUSES8921 followed 2025-10-09.

part_numbers.note: Original DIP8 socket-rolling part. Fakes reported (Nov 2023); treat new stock as suspect.
SOP8 (EMP8). Mouser lists it under NJR and Nisshinbo brands.
DFN8-X7 (ESON8-X7), added 2016-09-02. Assumed discontinued with the series.
SOP8 150 mil (EMP8). Direct replacement; vendor says specs and sound unchanged.
DIP8 in the Ver.0.2 preliminary only; never released. DIP 8920As are adapter modules.
Successor, new part number (2025-10-09). SOP8/DFN8; JPY 500/550 samples, 100k/month.

key_specs.value: J-FET input on a bipolar process

reputation.summary: Called the 'budget MUSES01' (Head-Fi) and a common cheap JFET upgrade for NE5532/NJM4580 sockets. Japanese listeners hear it as clean, dry and grain-free with a wide stage. diyAudio found only subtle gains over NE5532 in I/V use; Soomal called it thick and restrained. new_western_elec (2025) ranked it above MUSES8820 and OPA2604, below NL8802/NL8902.
typical_uses: Rolling in DACs, CD players, headphone amps, preamps
DAC post-filters and line outputs (Shanling M2, Magnetar UDP800)
Balanced headphone output (VentureCraft Vantam: two MUSES8920)
caveats: Needs at least ±3.5 V; maximum ±16 V (8920) or ±17 V (8920A). For low voltage, see MUSES8832.
MUSES8920D is discontinued and the 8920A is SMD-only; DIP sockets need an SOP8-to-DIP8 adapter.
new_western_elec heard 8920A vs 8920D differences (sub-bass, treble); one listener, adapter vs DIP confound.
Fake MUSES8920D parts reported (Nov 2023); buy from authorised channels.
Gains over NE5532 can be small; some find it cautious at the extremes. Soomal: MUSES DACs characterful, not outstanding.

counterfeit_notes: Fake MUSES8920D parts were reported in Nov 2023 (new_western_elec; AliExpress, Mercari), and 'new genuine' DIP8 lots still appear. A bare DIP8 marked 'MUSES8920A' is suspect: no AD was released. Compare font, logo and laser etch with genuine JRC parts.

silicon_changes.identification: 'A' suffix: MUSES8920AE/AE-TE1, AKX7; datasheet MUSES8920A (Ver.0.2, Ver.1.0). Marking not photo-verified. A vendor DIP8 must be old MUSES8920D; DIP 8920As are adapters (Akizuki g129639).
silicon_changes.summary: Nisshinbo ended MUSES8920 production and replaced it with MUSES8920A, stating electrical characteristics are unchanged and circuit and sound equivalent. No reason or PCN was found. Documented differences: DIP8 dropped and maximum supply raised from ±16 V to ±17 V. The THD headline gap reflects different test conditions.

spec_deltas.after: SOP8 JEDEC 150 mil/EMP8 (MUSES8920AE), DFN8-X7 (MUSES8920AKX7). DIP8 MUSES8920AD appears only in the Ver.0.2 preliminary.
The MUSES8920A datasheet quotes 0.0004% typ. at f=1 kHz, Av=+10, Vo=5 Vrms, RL=2 kOhm, and summaries also still cite 0.00004%. The test conditions differ, so this is not a confirmed spec change.
8.0 nV/rtHz, 25 V/us, 11 MHz, 5 pA (unchanged per vendor)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Vendor: none. new_western_elec (Nov 2025) heard deeper sub-bass, thinner bass line, less treble; Apr 2026: less depth, wider bandwidth. One listener; adapter confound.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – same pinout, vendor-stated equivalence, wider supply. DIP sockets need an adapter (height, stray capacitance).
silicon_changes.verification: Vendor equivalence statement, ±17 V range and 8920A THD test conditions confirmed. No reason or PCN found.

silicon_changes.identification: New part number with its own datasheet; covered by PHILE WEB (2025-10-14) and EDN Japan (2025-10-27). No 8920A discontinuation stated.
silicon_changes.summary: MUSES8921 is a new JFET dual based on the 2011 MUSES8920, with signal and power paths redesigned and element placement optimised using flagship MUSES techniques: a revised layout under a new number. Blogs call it the next step after MUSES8920A, which the vendor still lists.

spec_deltas.after: 8.0 nV/rtHz, 11.0 MHz, 25 V/us, 5 pA, 0.0004% THD (MUSES8921): identical headline figures

spec_deltas.before: MUSES8920/8920A signal and power path layout
spec_deltas.after: Signal and power paths redesigned and element placement optimised, per vendor press release

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Vendor claims better sound than MUSES8920. new_western_elec reviewed it in Apr 2026; verdict not captured.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – same headline specs and role; check package and pinout before swapping.
silicon_changes.verification: Vendor page, press coverage and X post confirm the redesign and specs. No 8920A discontinuation found.

revision_history.changes: MUSES8920 released, per Nisshinbo's 2025-10-09 MUSES8921 release.
Earliest dated English revision seen. No change log.
8 pages, 309 KB (alldatasheet 808066). Changes not shown; predates KX7.
KX7 (DFN8-X7) package added to MUSES8920 and MUSES8832.
Mouser copy 259012; reportedly lists KX7, so probably 2016-09 or later.
Mouser copy 1917228, probably ingested 2020 or later; possibly the last English revision.
Preliminary MUSES8920A datasheet; lists DIP8, SOP8 (EMP8) and DFN8-X7.
First production datasheet: AE and AKX7 orderable, AD not released. Probably around March 2024. Japanese Ver.1.0 at Akizuki.
MUSES8920 production ended; replaced by MUSES8920A with unchanged characteristics, circuit and sound. Date reported, no PCN found.
MUSES8921 (MUSES8921AN/GR, SOP8/DFN8) launched; MUSES8920 signal path, power path and element placement redesigned.
alldatasheet 2271958: 19 pages in Nisshinbo's long-form template vs 8 for MUSES8920_E. THD 0.0004%, 11 MHz, ±3.5 to ±17 V.
